parts:
Hey, using the second example in SO. 

ggplot(nbar.m, aes(x=row, y=variable, fill=value, alpha=valuep))+geom_tile()+scale_fill_gradientn(colours=c("red", "yellow", "green"))+theme_bw()+scale_alpha(na.value=0, range=c(1,0), guide=F)

Something like that. 

I reversed the scale_alpha for the p-value so the more significant stuff shows up brighter. I know the colors suck, but you can pick whatever you want using scale_gradientn(). I also hid the legend for alpha. I still think you should adjust the scale for alpha to have >.90 = dark, .70<=x<.90 = middle, and so on... maybe instead of continuous scale, use cut() here to set the alpha more precisely. 

Just an idea. What you need is something that you can look at and determine what's important. I happen to like the way this turned out (other than the colors being a bit too bright). 


B
